Replay

Scrapyard room recovery

3 min readOdin × GodotPage source ↓
On this page ↓
Lobby recoveryTakeover timers

The game uses the same model in standalone Session and coordinator-driven Room modes. Room owns the gameplay session, authenticated control connection, lease and prepared checkpoints. No alternate combat simulation is installed for migration.

The fixture starts three members, creates a long-lived zone and an airborne lob, and waits for the designated successor to hold a coordinator-prepared combat checkpoint. Planned handoff freezes at a final tick; abrupt mode kills the host process. The successor must install exactly the approved frame, including catalog, credit, cooldowns, effect/entity lifetime and query history, then continue the old lob and issue new casts. Surviving participants compare the entire world at one shared authoritative tick. In planned mode the old host returns as a client.

The shared Room driver separates gameplay freezing from control lease retirement. Its phase-aware permit prevents authoritative steps/commands while it renews the reservation long enough to transfer the final checkpoint. It drains unadmitted gameplay traffic without changing the frozen state or action ledger, allowing background acknowledgments through the shared router. Only the exact acknowledged, prepared final point permits retirement/release. Failure or successor loss leaves the old epoch fenced and enters the existing recovery policy.

Shell
nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/migration_run.sh
RSY_SLOW_BACKUP=1 REPLAY_MIGRATION_PHASE=planned nix develop --command bash examples/replay_scrapyard/migration_run.sh

The migration fixture deliberately adjusts initial positions, target health and ability duration/speed to keep observable combat state active. Slow mode reduces final-transfer bandwidth after the ordinary backup is prepared and requires the source to stay frozen for longer than one lease duration. These acceptance scenarios do not establish complete game recovery coverage, deployment, or full original-act parity.

Lobby recovery#

lobby_migration_run.sh runs planned and crash handoffs before starting the yard. It compares the complete installed staging frame, preserves names/loadouts and stable seats, gathers fresh readiness after reconnect, and starts the recovered game. The old host rejoins the planned case; all survivors compare the whole world.

World.host is the lobby's Start permission, not proof of simulation authority. A connected leader retains it. When that leader disconnects, the first connected seat receives it through the ordinary replayed roster step. Returning players do not preempt it. During current Room takeover the promoted seat remains connected while remote seats rejoin, so it becomes the lobby leader. If a future policy retains all memberships during recovery, this rule deliberately keeps the existing connected lobby leader. Dedicated worlds keep host == 0 and automatic start.

See recorded recovery evidence.

Takeover timers#

Content 0x5253435241503049 records the last observed authority epoch in World. Its versioned Model.authority policy applies the original succ_fixups rule on the first committed tick after a takeover: director rest and every existing mob's attack/reinforcement deadline become restored tick + 150. An Over-stage world also receives a fresh 150-tick dwell. Initial startup does not apply grace; repeated ticks in the same epoch do not extend it. Dedicated authorities work the same way even though both have playable seat zero.

Checkpoint installation remains exact. A second recovery before any resumed tick retains the pending reset, and an aborted simulation tick commits neither the reset nor the epoch stamp. Replaying recorded batches reproduces the policy.

This is a timer reset, not damage immunity. Movement, status effects, active boss telegraphs and popper proximity damage continue normally. Replay also retains its complete checkpoint projectiles, lobs and zones; the original's clearing of some transient pools is not reproduced. The active-combat fixture checks exact restored state followed by new shots, casts and kills in the same run, plus a new prepared backup to the demoted or returning infrastructure process.

Shell
REPLAY_DEDICATED_COMBAT_OUT=/absolute/fresh/output nix develop --command bash tests/replay_dedicated_combat/run.sh

This covers local native/Chrome planned and crash/return takeover with two servers and two players, forty enemies, 120 ms receive delay, and a maximum known rollback of 120 ticks. It does not establish a public-network, arbitrary-load or loss-rate guarantee. Original games remain separately runnable.
